To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the insensitive munition FOX-12 is photolabile, but it is also biodegradable, both aerobically and in the presence of sunlight, to form the same degradation products.
FOX-12, an energetic material, can be degraded effectively by a joint photodegradation and biodegradation process, which should not result in persistent contamination of surface water.
N-guanyl-urea-dinitromide (FOX- 12) is photolytically degraded to N₂O and NO₃(-) and that the guanyl-urea portion is microbially degraded to NH3, guanidine and CO2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fate and behavior of FOX-12 in surface waters.
the environmental behavior of FOX-12 and its photodegradation and biodegradation products.
the development of a novel technology for the degradation of FOX-12 and other energetic materials in surface waters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FOX-12 is not persistent under environmental conditions and is unlikely to be a source of groundwater contamination.
the joint process of photolysis and aerobic biodegradation is the most effective process for the complete degradation of FOX-12 in the environment.
the joint photomicrobial degradation process of FOX-12 in water is very efficient, and the resulting products are nontoxic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the joint photomicrobial degradation of FOX-12 is a viable process for the treatment of contaminated soils.
the joint photomicrobial approach is a promising tool for the degradation of energetic compounds.
the photolysis of FOX-12 in the environment would lead to the formation of guanylurea and dinitramide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dinitramine moiety of FOX-12 is not recalcitrant to microbial degradation and that its degradation products are innocuous.
, in addition to its high chemical stability, FOX-12 is photostable, which should allow its safe handling and use in the environment.
the photolysis of the dinitramidic component of FOX- 12 can be used as a pretreatment step for its biodegradation by strain VC1.
